name: Founders Fund
sectors: Generalist deep tech and software: defense (Anduril), space (SpaceX), data (Palantir), AI, crypto historically. Multi-stage.
stage: Unverified. Homepage shows no stage language, no pre-seed statement. Third-party guides describe it as multi-stage with rare early checks. Idea-stage acceptance not stated anywhere official.
geography: San Francisco, USA. Invests globally (not verified on site).
best_channel: Warm intro from a portfolio founder or co-investor; no public pitch form or email found on foundersfund.com (homepage fetched; /contact/ 404; /team/ returned HTTP 500).
notes: Homepage lists portfolio, team, manifesto, Anatomy of Next only. Beware: search results mix in Founders Fund Canada (foundersfund.ca, hello@foundersfund.ca), a different entity. Third-party guide (pitchprotocol.vc) says cold inbound conversion is very low. Portfolio includes crypto and fintech historically (not verified on site this session). Low fit for an idea-stage solo trading-bot pitch without an intro.

name: Conviction
sectors: AI-native companies, 'Software 3.0'. Portfolio: Harvey, Sierra, Cognition, Mistral, Baseten, Cartesia, HeyGen, Corridor.
stage: Early stage; site says 'We like to invest early, and are often the first investor.' Check range starts at $1M, so pre-seed possible but idea stage not explicitly stated.
best_channel: Direct DM or reply to Sarah Guo (@saranormous) or Mike Vernal (@mvernal) on X; no pitch form or pitch email on conviction.com (only jobs@conviction.com for hiring, seen in search snippet).
notes: Team: Sarah Guo, Mike Vernal (ex-Sequoia), Pranav Reddy, Bella Garcia-Camargo. Portfolio is AI infra and AI apps; no trading or prediction-market company seen on the homepage list. Launch post on Substack says founders 'are encouraged to reach out' (from search snippet, not fetched). /contact returned 404.

name: AI Grant
sectors: 'Anything that leverages AI models in a useful or engaging way.' AI apps and agents. Portfolio examples: Agency (AI agents for B2B customer success), Vapi (voice agent API), Hamming (voice agent testing).
stage: Pre-seed/seed explicitly: site says 'pre-seed/seed-stage startups', 'No credentials required', single founders eligible, prior fundraising acceptable. Idea stage not excluded.
check_size: $250,000 on a 'no cap, no discount MFN SAFE' plus $350,000 Azure credits and about $250,000 vendor credits
geography: Global; must form a Delaware corporation if accepted
pitch_email_or_form: Applications via aigrant.com during batch windows (site: 'Applications for Batch 4 are closed' at fetch time); application questions: support@aigrant.org (seen on aigrant.com)
best_channel: Watch aigrant.com and @aigrant on X for the next batch opening, then apply online; email support@aigrant.org for application questions.
cold_pitch_policy: Open application, no intro needed: 'No credentials required' (aigrant.com). No batch open at fetch time.
notes: Run by Hersh Desai and Lenny Bogdonoff; backed by Nat Friedman and Daniel Gross (nfdg.com, $10M). Distinct from aigrant.org (open-source grants). Strong fit for an AI-agent product; a trading bot must be framed as an AI-model product. Batch 5 status unknown as of 2026-09-02.

name: AI2 Incubator (now AI House)
sectors: AI-first startups, spun from Allen Institute for AI research
stage: Idea/incubation stage is the core program (third-party summaries; official site blocked this session). Reported: also invests in external pre-seed/seed companies following other lead investors. Not verified on official page.
check_size: Reported: up to $600,000 SAFE at $10M cap; initial $100k (solo) or $200k (team); incubation take is 7% common stock (from search snippets citing ai2incubator.com/faqs)
best_channel: Apply via the official site aihouse.vc / ai2incubator.com (application page could not be fetched; domain blocked in this session).
notes: Rebranded to AI House in June 2026 per search snippet. FAQ page URL: https://www.ai2incubator.com/faqs (not fetched). Prior angel or pre-seed funding does not disqualify. No trading or prediction-market portfolio seen. Verify terms on the live site before pitching.

name: Neo
sectors: Generalist tech, technical founders; supported by Microsoft and OpenAI
stage: Pre-seed and seed explicitly: Neo Accelerator is for 'pre-seed & seed cos' (Suzanne Xie tweet) and funding is 'competitive with a great pre-seed or seed round' (official Substack). At least one technical founder required.
check_size: $600K via an uncapped SAFE with a $10M floor valuation (official Substack); tweet wording: '$600K for 1.5% + an uncapped floor', $350K+ partner credits
geography: USA; 3-month program with bootcamp in Oregon, optional SF office space; Delaware C-Corp required before start (third-party)
pitch_email_or_form: https://neo.com/accelerator-apply (official application URL, linked from neo.substack.com)
best_channel: Apply online at neo.com/accelerator-apply when the yearly cohort opens (2025 deadline was mid-March; 2026 cycle dates not verified).
cold_pitch_policy: Open application form; no intro stated as required. No explicit cold-pitch statement found.
notes: neo.com pages are JavaScript-rendered; fetch returned only headers. Info sessions were run via calendly.com/neo-team. Founder Ali Partovi. No trading-specific portfolio seen. Application window timing must be checked on the site.

name: Pear VC
sectors: AI, Consumer, SaaS, Enterprise Tech, Healthcare, Deep Tech, Fintech, Biotech, Climate Tech (pear.vc/how-we-invest)
stage: Pre-seed and seed explicitly: 'We're specialists in pre-seed and seed.' Idea stage explicitly welcome for PearX: 'We encourage companies at the idea stage as well as teams already showing early traction to apply.'
geography: San Francisco and Menlo Park, CA; no applicant geography restriction stated
pitch_email_or_form: https://pear.vc/pearx-application (PearX W27 applications open; 'Regular Deadline is October 4th at 11:59PM PST')
best_channel: Apply to PearX via pear.vc/pearx-application before the October 4 regular deadline; subscribe to the monthly newsletter for program news.
cold_pitch_policy: Open application: 'We encourage companies at the idea stage as well as teams already showing early traction to apply.' (pear.vc/pearx-s26-applications). No statement on cold emails.
notes: PearX: 12-week program, $1M+ cloud credits. Partners Pejman Nozad and Mar Hershenson. pear.vc/pitch is a separate 'Pitch to Midas List Investors' event ($25k uncapped note, Airtable form). Contact page has addresses only, no email. Fintech is a listed sector.
sources: https://pear.vc/, https://pear.vc/how-we-invest/, https://pear.vc/pearx-application, https://pear.vc/pearx-s26-applications/, https://www.pear.vc/pitch, https://pear.vc/contact-us/

name: Afore Capital
sectors: Generalist pre-seed; third-party lists AI, fintech, healthcare, SaaS, consumer
stage: Pre-seed explicitly, pre-traction: site says invests in 'pre-traction, pre-everything companies'. Also runs a Founders-In-Residence program 'for those with raw ideas'.
geography: San Francisco, USA; US focus (geography not stated on page)
best_channel: Third-party guides cite a pitch form at afore.vc/pitch, but that URL returned 404 without www and the www domain was blocked; check the site nav for 'Pitch' or DM @gjain / @anamitra.
notes: Fund IV $185M (Feb 2025). Partners: Gaurav Jain, Anamitra Banerji. Also runs Afore Alpha and Afore x Gamma programs (URLs seen in search). Good stage fit for idea/pre-traction; pitch channel not verified.

name: Precursor Ventures
stage: Pre-seed and seed per site title 'Pre-Seed & Seed Stage Venture Capital'. Third-party: '$50K-500K in pre-PMF companies (as early as the idea-stage)'. Idea stage not verified on an official page this session (domain blocked).
pitch_email_or_form: https://precursorvc.com/startup/ (official page titled 'Startup Submission | Precursor Ventures' in search results; page not fetched, domain blocked)
best_channel: Submit the startup form at precursorvc.com/startup/; third-party guide says they accept direct form submissions and decide within one to two weeks.
cold_pitch_policy: no public statement found (official form exists; wording not fetched)
notes: Founder Charles Hudson. Runs a 'How to Raise a Pre-Seed Bootcamp' (precursorvc.com/preseedbootcamp/). Good stage fit. Verify the form and any sector exclusions on the live page.

name: Hustle Fund
sectors: Software startups. Excludes: 'pharmaceutical or medical device companies, art/film projects, land, restaurants / physical retail or traditional brick and mortar small businesses.' Fintech and crypto are not excluded.
stage: Pre-seed only, explicit: 'We invest in pre-seed rounds. Not seed. Not post-seed / mango seed. Pre-seed.' Sweet spot: 'companies that have built at least a minimum viable product (MVP).' Pure idea stage is below their sweet spot.
geography: 'Mostly the United States, Canada, and Southeast Asia.'
best_channel: Fill the 'Pitch us' Typeform on hustlefund.vc; then 30-60 minute call; decision 'usually within 48 hours after the call with a General Partner'.
cold_pitch_policy: 'Honestly, the fastest way to get an answer is to tell us what you're hustling. We read everything.' (hustlefund.vc/faq)
notes: GPs: Elizabeth Yin, Eric Bahn, Shiyan Koh. Champion model, no all-partner meeting. Acceptance under 1%. Site: 'You don't need perfect metrics, a famous network, or a 47-slide deck.' Strong fit once an MVP bot exists.

name: Boost VC
sectors: 'Sci-Fi future': robotics, AI, bio, health, materials, space tech, computing, crypto, ocean tech, AR/VR, climate, energy. Portfolio: Coinbase, Etherscan, Deepgram.
stage: Pre-seed explicit: 'We Lead Pre-Seed Rounds'. Idea stage covered by '$50k Fellowship checks for founders who just need a bit of capital to get started, but are too early to raise a full pre-seed round.'
geography: Global: 'yes, we invest globally'; based in San Mateo, CA; free housing at Draper University for visiting founders
best_channel: Apply via the fillout forms on boost.vc/faq; intro optional.
cold_pitch_policy: 'Please get in touch with us via intro from someone in our network or apply through our $500k Application.' (boost.vc/faq)
notes: Adam Draper (MD), Brayton Williams. 70+ startups per year. Crypto is an explicit sector; Coinbase and Etherscan in portfolio. info@boost.vc appears only in third-party sources, not verified on site. Good fit for crypto/prediction-market angle.

name: Lerer Hippeau
sectors: AI, fintech, biotech, food tech, real estate, energy, manufacturing, drone delivery. Fintech examples: Guideline (acquired by Gusto), On Me.
stage: Site news shows seed and Series A rounds. Third-party (vcsheet, superscout) says pre-seed and seed. Pre-seed/idea acceptance not verified on the official site.
best_channel: No pitch form or email on the site (homepage and /team fetched; /contact 404); warm intro or DM to a partner on X.
notes: Managing Partners: Ben Lerer, Eric Hippeau, Graham Brown; Partner Isabelle Phelps. NYC-network focus. Weaker fit for an idea-stage, non-NYC trading-bot founder.

name: Bloomberg Beta
sectors: Future of work, machine intelligence, 'companies that make business work better'. Criteria file: 'without being in financial services'. Avoids e-commerce and entertainment.
stage: Seed/first check: 'We strongly prefer to be the first money into a company, and to invest as early in the startup's life as possible.' No minimum check size; 'have written checks as small as $25,000'. Idea stage not excluded.
check_size: Typical first check $500k-$1M; range $300k up to $1M; no minimum
geography: 'We mainly invest in the San Francisco Bay Area and New York', 'consider backing founders anywhere in North America'
best_channel: Find a mutual connection; the manual says 'Wouldn't you rather try to find someone in common?' If cold, show you read the manual.
cold_pitch_policy: 'Should you send us a cold email or DM? Probably not.' (github.com/Bloomberg-Beta/Manual, 1 - Manual.md)
notes: WARNING: the investing criteria explicitly exclude financial services. A trading bot or prediction-market product is likely out of scope. $75M seed fund capitalized by Bloomberg. Team: Roy Bahat, James Cham, Karin Klein, Angela Martin, Lori Berenberg. Manual is public on GitHub.

name: Susa Ventures
sectors: Third-party: enterprise software, fintech, healthcare, logistics, infrastructure, dev tools, frontier tech. Portfolio includes Robinhood (not verified on site this session).
stage: Pre-seed and seed explicit: 'invests in pre-seed and seed rounds, backing companies at their earliest stages and beyond' (susaventures.substack.com/about). Idea stage not explicitly stated.
best_channel: Third-party guides cite pitches@susaventures.com; this was NOT seen on an official page (site pages beyond the homepage were blocked or 404). DM a partner on X or verify the email on the live site.
notes: Team: Chad Byers, Pratyush Buddiga, Misha Gordon-Rowe, Shaheer Sandhu. Blog at susaventures.substack.com. Fintech is a listed sector per third parties, which fits a trading product.
